summary: BA's analysis is technically accurate and evidence-backed, with two minor scope classifications worth flagging (kbd as Should-have, ordered list styling as Could-have) that do not invalidate the spec overall.

evidence_quality.notes: Every claim about missing primitives independently verified by QA via direct Read of the four source files plus Grep pattern 'blockquote|strikethrough|~~|task.list|\[x\]|\[ \]|<kbd|<|&|>' scoped to packages/happy-app/sources/components/markdown/ which returned zero matches — confirming BA's claim of total absence.
verified_claims: parseMarkdown.ts:42-43 — MarkdownSpan.styles union = ('italic' | 'bold' | 'semibold' | 'code')[] — confirmed exact match, 'strikethrough' absent
parseMarkdown.ts:3-39 — MarkdownBlock union includes text/header/list/numbered-list/code-block/mermaid/latex/horizontal-rule/options/table/image — confirmed NO 'blockquote' or 'task-list' member

parseMarkdownBlock.ts:163-171 — list branch uses `trimmed.startsWith('- ')` and `lines[index].trim().startsWith('- ')` — confirmed trim() kills indentation info, no task-list detection, no depth tracking
parseMarkdownBlock.ts:53-188 — full function scanned — confirmed NO '>'-prefix branch, NO HTML entity decode pass

MarkdownView.tsx (760 lines) — grep for Blockquote|TaskList|strikethrough|line-through|decode|entity|kbd|checkbox (case-insensitive) returned zero matches — confirmed NO RenderBlockquoteBlock, NO RenderTaskListBlock, NO strikethrough style, NO entity decode

scope_alignment.notes: BA preserved the user's verbatim in `requirement.original` AND in `requirements_decomposition[].source_phrase`. BA's claim 'headings H1-H6 already work, user was pointing at numbered list items' is independently verified by QA reading parseMarkdownBlock.ts:62-67 (header loop) and parseMarkdownSpans.ts is used for header content — the code path DOES handle # through ###### correctly. The user's `包括一级标题二级标题等` (including H1 H2 etc) is an example list, not an exclusive list, and the reference screenshots cited in §5.17 clearly show numbered-title lines (1.1, 1.2, 1.3) being the failing content, not `# heading` syntax. BA's interpretation is defensible and is explicitly disclosed in the evidence section rather than silently re-scoped.
observations: BA correctly keeps R6 (headings) in Must-have as 'verify no regression' — NOT dropped from scope
BA's 'user confusion with numbered list items' hypothesis is backed by the reference screenshot content and by code evidence (lines 62-67 work); it is NOT an undocumented scope shrink

investigation_completeness.notes: All 7 primitives listed in §5.17 extracted acceptance points are addressed in BA's requirements. Classification concerns exist but do not constitute missing investigation — BA identified ALL missing primitives and mapped each to an AC.
classification_observations: §5.17 point 7 groups <kbd> and </> entities together in the user's requirement. BA split them: entities in R5 (must-have) but <kbd> in R8 (should-have). User's verbatim treats them as the same complaint — classifying them at different priority levels is a minor risk that dev/QA should be aware of. If only R5 is implemented, the user may still complain that <kbd> renders raw. BA's AC7 acknowledges this by accepting EITHER keycap rendering OR clean literal decoded text — the latter is achieved via HTML-tag stripping, which is a reasonable fallback.

§5.17 point 5 (ordered list visual styling) was classified as R10 could-have. Parser handling of ordered lists works (verified lines 148-159), so user complaint is cosmetic. BA explicitly labels this 'L1 cosmetic gap, not L3 parser gap' in evidence — defensible but does mean dev can legitimately skip it.

affected_file_accuracy.notes: All four affected file paths and their stated line ranges verified accurate against actual source.

verified_files.note: BA said 188 — actual is 189 (off by 1, trivial)

objections.issue: §5.17 point 7 groups <kbd> and HTML entities as one complaint item. BA split them into R5 (must-have, entities) and R8 (should-have, kbd). If dev skips R8, the user's verbatim is only partially met. Recommend upgrading R8 to Must-have OR ensuring AC7's 'clean literal decoded text' fallback path is implemented even in the Must-have scope.
objections.impact: Low — BA's AC7 explicitly accepts two alternative implementations (keycap style OR clean decoded literal), and the simpler fallback can piggyback on R5 entity-decode + HTML-tag stripping.

objections.issue: §5.17 point 5 (ordered list visual styling) is only Could-have (R10). User complained 'ordered list should render with list-item styling (not as two plain text lines)'. BA correctly notes parser works, so this is cosmetic, but user complaint is NOT null.
objections.impact: Low — parser already handles ordered lists correctly; visual styling is an incremental improvement. Dev can legitimately defer.

objections.issue: BA's headings-already-work claim is based on code inspection (lines 62-67), not Playwright observation. BA disclosed this as 'inferred' in `evidence_type`. QA should verify no heading regression during implementation QA.
objections.impact: None — BA was transparent about inference vs observation

strengths: BA verified each missing primitive by reading source at exact line ranges (not just grepping)
BA disclosed the 'inferred' evidence type rather than claiming observed evidence
BA preserved the user's verbatim in requirement.original AND each requirements_decomposition source_phrase
BA identified the shared-code dependency with §5.16 and flagged merge-order coordination
BA's edge-case analysis (~~ inside code span, task list before plain list,   in RN, shared type union) is thorough
BA's affected file line ranges are accurate to within one line
BA added R10 (could-have) specifically to address the ordered-list visual styling the user complained about, rather than silently dropping it
recommendation: ACCEPT BA spec. Forward to dev. Dev should (1) prioritize a minimal <kbd> handling as part of R5 entity-decode path to satisfy user's verbatim, and (2) consider R10 (ordered list cosmetic styling) if cheap to include alongside R3 nested-list change since both touch RenderListBlock.
